# Independent reference data

`opposition_2018.txt` is copied unchanged from Astronomy Engine's published test data:
https://github.com/cosinekitty/astronomy/blob/master/generate/longitude/opposition_2018.txt

The equinox test uses the published entry `2024-03-20T03:06Z Equinox` from:
https://github.com/cosinekitty/astronomy/blob/master/generate/seasons/seasons.txt

At opposition the geocentric ecliptic longitude difference from the Sun is 180 degrees. At the March equinox the Sun's tropical longitude is zero. Tolerances allow minute-rounded times and the library's model error. These checks cover Sun, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn. Absolute fixtures for all seven planets and the mean node are described below.

Reference fixture license: MIT, Copyright (c) 2019-2025 Don Cross.

## Native Swiss reference corpus

`swiss-native.json` contains 64 extracted, pre-existing native gcc/x86-64 Swiss Ephemeris 2.10.03 results. The pinned source URL and original compressed-file SHA-256 are recorded in the JSON. Expected values are not generated by the WASM implementation under test.

- Tropical: January 15, 12:00 UT1 in 1700, 1900, 2000 and 2100; geocentric apparent ecliptic/equinox of date, Moshier + speed (flags 260), seven planets and mean node; tolerance 0.0000001 degrees.
- Sidereal: June 15, 12:00 UT1 in those years; Lahiri mode 1, Swiss-file + speed + sidereal (flags 65794), seven planets; tolerance 0.002 degrees (7.2 arcseconds) allows the reference Swiss-file versus application Moshier model difference.
- Ayanamsha: same June dates, Lahiri `swe_get_ayanamsa_ex_ut`, nutation included; tolerance 0.0000001 degrees. Julian dates in each record are UT1, not UTC or TT.

These fixtures independently check the browser port against native compilation of the same astronomical algorithm; they are not an independent astronomical theory. The opposition/equinox sources above provide additional external event checks. Boundary tests separately cover all signs, nakshatras, padas and exact node opposition.

Swiss corpus/source license: AGPL-3.0-or-later. Official model and coordinate documentation: https://www.astro.com/swisseph/swephprg.htm and https://www.astro.com/swisseph/swephinfo_e.htm .

## Lagna and whole-sign houses

`houses-native.json` extracts 36 pre-existing tropical whole-sign ascendants from the same pinned native-C corpus, at multiple dates and northern/southern/eastern/western locations. Each timestamp is JD UT1; latitude is north-positive and longitude east-positive. Tests compare the sidereal ascendant plus apparent Lahiri ayanamsha with the published tropical ascendant (tolerance 0.000001°). Ayanamsha itself is covered by the independent native fixtures above. These checks validate the port/conventions, not an independent astronomical theory.

House boundaries are sign starts, not the exact Lagna degree. Assignment uses sidereal signs. This release deliberately leaves houses unavailable for |latitude| >= 66° rather than claiming verified polar conventions.

## Vimshottari reference rules

Sequence, lengths and proportional subdivisions are documented by the implementing publisher at https://samvat.in/learn/vimshottari-dasha/ and https://jyotipy.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/dasha.html (accessed 2026-09-22). We use 365.25 uniform days per year; different year conventions produce different dates. Nine complete major periods are shown from the true start of the birth major period, not 120 years after birth. Intervals include their start and exclude their end.

Hand-derived fixtures (not generated by our utility): for birth 2000-01-01 00:00 UTC and Moon 0° sidereal, Ketu ends after 2556.75 days on 2006-12-31 18:00 UTC. Ketu/Ketu lasts 149.14375 days and ends 2000-05-29 03:27 UTC. At Ashwini's midpoint, half the seven years remain, ending 2003-07-02 09:00 UTC. Tests additionally cover every nakshatra boundary, subperiod continuity and a complete 43830-day cycle. These verify traditional timing arithmetic; they do not validate predictions.
